candidate.educational_objective: Apply the cited evidence to recognize the uniquely safest or most accurate nursing response in the clinical situation tested by V2-Q0141.

options.A: I will compare each reading with a population-predicted value because my own best measurement should not be used to guide an individualized action plan.
options.B: I will compare readings with my established personal best and follow the written action-plan zones and instructions when values fall from that baseline.
options.C: I need to measure peak flow only during a severe attack because routine or symptom-triggered trends cannot provide useful information about worsening control.
options.D: If my peak flow falls, I will ignore symptoms and use the number alone because action plans should not incorporate clinical changes or medication instructions.

candidate.rationale: CDC asthma action-plan guidance uses individualized green, yellow, and red zones and expresses peak expiratory flow relative to the person's best peak flow. The client should compare readings with the established personal best and follow the written action-plan instructions rather than rely on a population value or an isolated number.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC Living with Asthma page, Asthma Action Plan Green/Yellow/Red Zone section: peak flow zones are expressed as percentages of the individual's best peak flow. Page dated May 4, 2026; reviewed 2026-08-14.
